newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: PSC Industries ups Naval Dockyard stake.
newsitem.headline: PSC Industries ups Naval Dockyard stake.

text.p: Malaysia's PSC Industries Bhd has proposed to raise its shareholding in Naval Dockyard Sdn Bhd to 58 percent through various proposed acquisitions.

PSC Industries said in a statement issued late on Monday that it was acquiring 100 percent interest in Safe Era Sdn Bhd and the remaining 50 percent equity in Suria Barisan Sdn Bhd which it does not own.
Safe Era holds 10 percent in Naval Dockyard and Suria Barisan eight percent.

PSC Industries, which now holds 28 percent stake in Naval Dockyard, had in December proposed to increase its shareholding to 44 percent through its subsidiary, Penang Shipbuilding and Construction Sdn Bhd.
PSC Industries will pay 40.8 million ringgit for Safe Era and 16.32 million for the 50 percent stake in Suria Barisan.
The company said the proposed acquisitions would enable PSC Industries to assume greater control of Naval Dockyard which was expected to contribute significantly to its long-term profitability.
Naval Dockyard is a shipping and shipyard company which was privatised by the Malaysian government to a consortium led by PSC Industries.

The privatisation of Naval Dockyard included a contract to build 27 patrol vessels for the Malaysian navy estimated to be worth more than 5.6 billion ringgit, and the maintenance of the vessels for 15 years. ($1 = 2.49 ringgit) -- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-230 8911)
